slot.brief: Series LCR at resonance (circuit given): state resonance condition and compute rms current, or identify power factor and phase relation between V and I at resonance.

stem: A series LCR circuit is connected to a $120$ V rms AC source and operates at resonance, as shown in the figure. If the resistance is $40\ \Omega$, what is the rms current?

verdicts.working: At resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, so the impedance is just R = 40 Ω. Thus I_rms = 120 V / 40 Ω = 3 A.

working:
At resonance, $Z=R=40\ \Omega$.
$I_{\rm rms}=\dfrac{V_{\rm rms}}{Z}=\dfrac{120}{40}=3$ A.

Independent check: At resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, so the impedance is just R = 40 Ω. Thus I_rms = 120 V / 40 Ω = 3 A.
solution:
At resonance, the inductive and capacitive reactances cancel, so $Z=R=40\,\Omega$.
$$I_{\rm rms}=\frac{V_{\rm rms}}{Z}=\frac{120}{40}=3\,\text{A}$$

draft.stem: A series LCR circuit is connected to a $120$ V rms AC source and operates at resonance, as shown in the figure. If the resistance is $40\ \Omega$, what is the rms current?

figure.description: Draw a single closed series loop containing, in order, an AC source labeled '$120$ V rms', a resistor labeled '$40\ \Omega$', an inductor labeled '$L$', and a capacitor labeled '$C$'. Label the circuit 'at resonance'. Use standard circuit symbols and show connecting wires.

draft.distractor_notes: A: Doubles the impedance; C: Uses an incorrect impedance; D: Confuses peak and rms voltage.
